text: hey thank you for the kind words and for the great question I'm not aware of any references to cannabis in the Hebrew
Bible I know there is a theory that Kane bosum is a precursor etymologically to the word cannabis I have not been
convinced of that yet however we do have two pieces of archaeological data that demonstrate the use of cannabis both
medically and ritually in ancient Israel and the first comes from the first temple period judahite Temple at a rod
in the southern desert the holy of holies at this Temple was discovered along with a standing Stone and two incense altars a small one and a large
one and both had burnt substances on top of them and those substances were tested and the substance on top of the smaller
incense altar contained THC CBD and CBN so cannabis was being used in the
incense altars to obviously enhance the ritual experience at least at a rod and probably at other temples and perhaps
even including the Jerusalem Temple the journal T aiv published an article on this in 2020 the other example comes from a
little further north in the northern Hill Country a burial of a 14-year-old girl who died in childbirth where her
lungs were they discovered a powdery substance that they tested and showed to contain THC and so the going theory is
that she was given cannabis to treat the pain of this difficult delivery that ultimately would take her life and this
was briefly discussed about 30 years ago in an article in nature so we can demonstrate both medicinally and
ritually cannabis was a part of ancient Israelite life
